nodes.name: Synthetic Data Generation
nodes.procedure: Define a generative process to synthesize diverse tabular datasets using structural causal models (SCMs). Sample high-level hyperparameters including dataset size, number of features, and difficulty. Construct a directed acyclic graph (DAG) using the growing network with redirection sampling method. Propagate initialization data (Normal, Uniform, or Mixed noise) through root nodes. Apply computational mappings at edges including small neural networks, categorical feature discretization, decision trees, and Gaussian noise injection. Extract intermediate representations at sampled feature and target nodes. Apply post-processing including Kumaraswamy feature warping, quantization, and missing value masking.

unit_operations.name: Graph Structure Sampling
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: We sample these graphs using the growing network with redirection sampling method, a preferential attachment process that generates random scale-free networks.

unit_operations.name: Data Propagation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: As these data traverse the edges of the computational graph, we apply a diverse set of computational mappings... adding Gaussian noise.

unit_operations.name: Post-processing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: This includes warping with the Kumaraswamy distribution, introducing complex nonlinear distortions and quantization mimicking discretized features.

nodes.name: Foundation Model Pre-training
nodes.procedure: Train the transformer-based PFN to predict masked targets of synthetic datasets using cross-entropy loss. Use the Adam optimizer with linear warmup and cosine annealing. Training is conducted for approximately 2,000,000 steps with a batch size of 64 datasets on a node with eight Nvidia RTX 2080 Ti GPUs. The model learns to approximate the posterior predictive distribution across the corpus of synthetic tasks. The architecture employs two-way attention (inter-feature and inter-sample) and half-precision layer norms to optimize memory.

nodes.name: Model Fine-tuning
nodes.procedure: Perform fine-tuning on specific dataset classes or related datasets to improve performance on specialized tasks. Unlike tree-based methods, the neural architecture of TabPFN enables weight updates on specific data distributions (e.g., sine curves with varying offsets or medical diagnosis tasks). This allows the transfer of knowledge even when labels differ significantly between fine-tuning and test tasks.
